property_summary: After a successful lockInGuess with some hash, calling settle in the same block must revert (because settle requires block.number > the locked block), and the locked-in block was exactly the current block plus one.
After a successful lockInGuess, the caller's stored guess block is always exactly one greater than the block number at which lockInGuess was called, so settle in the same block must revert.
After a successful lockInGuess, the stored guess block equals the block number at which lockInGuess was called plus one, and an immediate settle call in the same block must revert.
After a successful lockInGuess, the caller's guess block is exactly one greater than the current block number, so settle reverts in the same block.
Once a player locks in a guess, settle() can only be called after the lock block has passed, and a correct guess pays exactly 2 ether while an incorrect guess pays 0 ether.

After a successful settle(), if the caller's guess was correct the contract pays exactly 2 ether, and after any settle() (successful or reverted) the caller's lock is cleared (calling settle again reverts) or no payout more than once is possible.

After a player locks in a guess and the lock block has been passed, the first settle() call either clears the lock (success) or reverts due to the block condition; in either case, the lock is never left in a state where settle() is callable twice successfully.
After a player locks in a guess, at most one settle() call can succeed; a second settle() must revert because the lock is cleared after the first call.
